headline: Pittsburgh Penguins Ville Koivunen’s NHL Performance is Beginning to Impress

paragraphs.text: An overtime goal against the Nashville Predators has made many realize that Ville Koivunen projection for his future NHL performance is clearly making him a fixture in the lineup. He is showing a well-round game, early on in his NHL career. Let’s discuss the details.
An Expected Contract with an Unexpected Price

A 23-year-old restricted free agent with just 47 NHL games under his belt was the resume Ville Koivunen possessed when general manager Kyle Dubas and the Pittsburgh Penguins decided to extend him eight years on a contract with an average annual value of $4 million. He had scored just two NHL goals at the time of the deal.
The Penguins have re-signed restricted free agent forward Ville Koivunen to an eight-year contract.— Pittsburgh Penguins (@penguins) August 6, 2026
AHL-Level Excellence and Arriving Just When He’s Needed

While Koivunen hadn’t yet lit up the NHL, he has long established himself as a top-level producer at the AHL level. Coming over from the Carolina Hurricanes as part of the Jake Guentzel trade, Koivunen quickly established himself with the Penguins’ farm team, the Wilkes-Barre/Scranton Penguins. After scoring 21 goals and 56 points in 2024-25, a 13-goal, 43-point season in 2025-26 meant that Koivunen had done all he could at that level and just needed to find a way to break into the NHL lineup.

His chance came as a result of a ton of injuries to Pittsburgh’s forward group. Veterans like Evgeni Malkin, Rickard Rakell, as well as younger players like last year’s star acquisition Egor Chinakhov, have all found themselves falling out of the lineup. A team already struggling to find their flow, the Penguins responded to this adversity with increased opportunity for players like Koivunen, another trade acquisition, Rutger McGroarty, who came over from the Winnipeg Jets, and also, the Hendrix Lapierre trade, who was with the Washington Capitals. A general theme has emerged, and spots opening up for players like Koivunen and Lapierre have led to unexpected chemistry between the pair. They’ve been dominant in their time together.

Ville Koivunen’s overtime winner may have put more attention on his performance, but he’s already been playing better than the credit he’s given for this season. A speedy and skilled winger capable of playing some defence, the biggest criticisms of Koivunen’s game have been his lack of physicality and his decision-making. The young forward would routinely get knocked off the puck when in transition or driving into opposing zones. Additionally, his decision-making had been lacking, with less-than-ideal passes to teammates or driving at inopportune times. This season, it’s evident Koivunen has worked hard on these issues, as he’s consistently able to make the smart play, using his speed and skill to keep possession or get his linemates better opportunities.

With two goals and five points in 14 games, Koivunen has made a marked difference wherever he’s placed in the lineup, playing stout defence and acting as a fast, speedy transition winger. His latest goal was a game-winner in overtime, a clean shot after extended time holding onto the puck that beat elite goaltender Juuse Saros after making a fantastic move to get away from the Nashville defence.

With injuries and rumours of veterans on the way out, the Penguins are primed to get younger and need players to emerge as staples in the line-up. Pittsburgh is not an organization that is interested in a full teardown rebuild just yet, and still needs players that can produce, develop, and become legitimate threats. Ville Koivunen seems primed to finally establish himself as one such player this season. Having cleaned up his deficiencies and focused on his strengths has evolved Koivunen’s game. Meanwhile, Head Coach Dan Muse and the coaching staff have all shown belief in the young star, with time on the power play, penalty kill, and overtime. In the 2026-27 NHL season, Ville Koivunen is establishing himself in the NHL.
